name: Baconnaise

ingredients.name: water, plus more to correct consistency

instructions.primary_message: Combine bacon fat and canola oil in 2-cup liquid measuring cup. Whisk to combine.

Add egg yolks, Dijon mustard, mayonnaise, and water to bowl of food processor (see note). Run processor for 5 seconds to combine. Scrape down sides of processor bowl with rubber spatula. With processor running, slowly drizzle fat into bowl in a thin, steady stream, stopping and scraping down sides as necessary. Add lemon juice, salt, and pepper to taste, and adjust consistency with water until thick, smooth, and creamy, but not mouth-coatingly waxy. Stir in cumbled bacon bits and sliced scallions, if using. Store in refrigerator in air-tight container for up to two weeks.

description: We're still betting that this meaty mayo will be the new "it" condiment. Whip some up today for a glimpse of our bright future.
notes:
Optional or for serving: 2 tablespoons mayonnaise (optional, see note); 2 scallions, white and green parts, finely sliced (optional)

Notes: This mayonnaise can be made with vegetable oil in place of the rendered animal fat - though flavor will suffer.
For insurance, I add jarred mayonnaise to the food processor at the start, which makes it easier to create a stable emulsion. If you are an experienced mayonnaise-maker who has no problems with mayonnaise breaking on you, you may omit the jarred mayonnaise.
The mayonnaise can also be made in a bowl with a whisk.

Make-ahead and storage: Store in refrigerator in an air-tight container for up to two weeks.
author: J. Kenji López-Alt
